correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge3\), integer \(1\le q\le n\), and real \(\kappa,w>0\), the grounded clique inverse is a diagonal-plus-rank-one matrix whose scalar denominator is \(q(1/n-1/(n+\kappa))>0\). The anomalous link changes the inverse trace by \((1-w)s/[1-(1-w)r]\). Three endpoint-orbits exhaust all feasible leader sets. Their exact \((r,s)\) pairs yield strict weak-link dominance, reinforced-link strict comparison of \(j=1\) against \(j=2\), and the complete \(j=0\) versus \(j=1\) affine sign boundary including ties. For \((n,q,\kappa)=(5,3,10)\), the exact transition is \(w=27/22\). The independent direct-matrix exact-rational checker reproduced 495 parameter choices and 7470 leader sets; the unrestricted conclusion follows from the symbolic proof, not the finite tests.

originality.rationale: The literature establishes the objective, its general inverse/resistance representations and computational leader-selection methods. Materially inspected primary sources solve different graph families, cardinalities or leader-gain limits; none gives the exact all-cardinality finite-gain optimization for a complete graph with one arbitrary exceptional edge. The proof derives a three-orbit sign classification for all \(n,q,\kappa,w\), including the sharp \(27/22\) transition. Targeted semantic index searches for edge-defective cliques, grounded trace inverse and rank-one formulations returned no direct covering claim. The standard inversion lemma is explicitly excluded from the originality claim; unindexed coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased specialized weighted-clique lemma could cover all or part of the new law.

value.rationale: A single degraded or strengthened communication link is a motivated perturbation of a maximally symmetric noisy consensus network. The exact classification holds for unbounded graph order and every finite leader cardinality, positive gain and link conductance and includes all ties. Weakening produces a structural reversal between one and two leaders, and reinforcing exhibits an exact gain-dependent phase switch with a rational worked instance. The result identifies optimal sensor/leader response to a localized link anomaly; its content is the new orbit-optimizer law rather than a generic matrix inverse or a narrow arbitrary numerical instance.
